text: Databases store structured data so it can be queried quickly. Tables hold rows of records with typed columns. An index is a data structure, often a B-tree, that maps key values to row locations. Without an index, a query scans every row; with one, it jumps straight to matches. Indexes speed reads but slow writes and consume space. Good schema design balances both, and query…
